title: Salesforce Koa: An Enterprise Language Model for Agentic Tool Use
summary: This method replaces prompt engineering and supervised fine-tuning for tool-use behavior with RL post-training (GRPO) on a 120B open-weight model, using rewards grounded in simulated multi-turn workflow tasks derived from declarative agent specifications. The cost is substantial: reinforcement-learning post-training of a 120B-parameter model, plus a simulation and reward-verification pipeline, is far beyond a single 24 GB GPU and requires dedicated training infrastructure. What can fail is reward misspecification—models can overfit to synthetic persona-conditioned simulations and tool-call success signals that do not match real production workflows, degrading general-purpose behavior.
rationale: The training recipe is out of reach for constrained infrastructure, but the specification-to-simulation-to-reward design pattern is worth tracking as a template for evaluating and improving tool use with smaller models or API-based agents.
technique: Specification-driven GRPO post-training for agentic tool use
